dog_description_omission: New early dog and common dog suffix are correctly identified by direct raw-feature readout. Neutral V only mentions garden/tree/house/fence; both text readers output none. Omission in a short caption does not establish visual absence.
cat_description: V mentions cat and additionally a small bird landing on its back, not seen in the manually inspected input. Original R chooses bird; frozen candidate R chooses cat. Correct final subject does not make the entire generated caption factual.
direct_semantics: All direct normal outputs are allowed short aliases; no full-sentence scoring discrepancy in this stage.
causal_scope: Direct raw features pass both new early animals and both swaps with identical suffix, demonstrating dependence on supplied early evidence under manual intervention/time-only selection. Caption bridge fails the strict pair. This is not a forest compression, semantic retrieval, or natural long-video benchmark.
decision: Keep the frozen local/plain reader as optional diagnostic. Preserve original visual features; do not make neutral generated captions the sole evidence or infer absence from omission. Do not add a post-output adaptive route choosing whichever arm happens to be correct.
